# Why now

> I asked Claude to publish our Search Console table, and it wants to go through steps first. Can't I just publish it now and describe it later?
> — A colleague from SEO, the first time they publish a Resource

Search Console impressions, whole site is in the Collection Attraction at 2 · Described: the Data Team described in dbt how it is built, and only SEO and the Data Team see it. Its intended use and one pitfall were written before; the rest of its card is empty. Data Hub refuses to publish a Resource whose card says nothing of what it is for, where it trips people up and what it does not hold, in Claude as in Data Hub itself.

Promise: the steps between a described Resource and a published one, why they come in this order, and how you pick them up again.

# Core idea

The **Owner Journey** takes a Resource from described to published one step at a time, in a fixed order: first what it is, then how to use it and where it trips people up, and last what you vouch for.

## At Immoscoop

Claude takes the colleague of SEO through Search Console impressions, whole site, one step at a time. First what it is: a look at the data together, the Business Description, then the Key Fields and their descriptions, before those of the other fields, as colleagues and the EDA start from the Key Fields. Then how to use it and where it trips people up: the intended use, the pitfalls, and the Known Gaps with the day it is reliable since. The Parameters, what the Data Admin records and the open Questions and Signals come next; advised, or needed later for the EDA, they hold nothing up. Last the card is read back and published, as the declaration vouches for every text before it. For each text Claude says where its proposal comes from, and writes it only once the colleague agrees: from then on the text is theirs. The colleague stops after the intended use. Three days later a colleague of SEO asks Claude, in a new conversation, where they were, and goes on at the pitfalls: the Owner Journey is kept with the Resource, not with the conversation.

# Check your understanding

## You described half of a Resource with Claude last week. Today a colleague of your Owner Unit opens a new conversation about it. Where does the journey go on?

- [ ] At the start: the journey lived in your conversation
- [ ] Nowhere: only whoever started it goes on with it
- [x] Where you stopped: the journey is kept with the Resource, for every member of the Owner Unit

Why: the journey is read from the Resource, from what its card holds and what the Owner Unit said, never from a conversation. What you went through stays done, with who did it and when.

## The card of a Resource has everything but its intended use and its Parameters. What holds up its publication?

- [ ] Both: every step of the journey is done before a Resource is published
- [ ] Neither: ticking the declaration covers what is still open
- [x] The intended use, which is required; the Parameters are advised and hold nothing up

Why: each step is required to publish, needed later for the EDA, or advised. The catalogue refuses a publication while a required step is open, in Data Hub as in Claude, and both show the same list of what is open and what is only advised.

## A colleague of your Owner Unit would rather confirm the card first, so that colleagues see the Resource sooner, and write its texts afterwards. Why does the journey not go that way?

- [ ] It does: the order of the steps is only a suggestion
- [ ] Because the Data Team approves each text first
- [x] Because the declaration vouches for every text on the card, so the texts come first and what you vouch for last

Why: publishing confirms what the card says, and from then on everyone who sees the Collection reads it; a Publication is not undone. Confirming a card that is still empty would vouch for nothing, so the journey puts it last.

# You can now

ask "which required steps are still open, and where did we stop?" before you set out to publish a Resource, and go through its steps in their order, in one conversation or several.
